review_scope: External drift supplement, not artifacts of the original locked tree

observations.statement: Desktop interactions are described for local macOS and Windows sessions; GUI-only workflows are examples, not evidence of support for remote sessions or all operating systems.
The status command reports plugin, MCP server and associated skill enablement; enablement status alone does not prove effective application access or completed work.
Enablement persists a local preference and activates the bundled plugin, but cannot override an organization-managed disablement; macOS needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.
Requests should identify outcome, applications and constraints. The illustrative read-only prompt is not authorization to control an application in this review.
The active CLI permission mode controls approval prompting. Current-session permission and saved future-session approval are distinct choices, with decline/cancel available.
Saved application approval also applies to the app on the same computer. Confirm requested application and action; explicit deny rules take precedence.
The documented CLI interruption uses two Escape presses; this is an operation interrupt, not proof that permission has been revoked.
Disabling the feature should be followed by checking plugin and MCP-server status; neither operation was executed here.
Troubleshooting distinguishes account/platform/session eligibility, plugin enablement, MCP connectivity and both macOS permissions; a single enabled component does not establish full readiness.
The app supports the described desktop interaction capability in local macOS and Windows sessions; the concept page supplies broader limitations.

App enablement and macOS prerequisites are separate controls: Accessibility supports application control and Screen Recording supports visual inspection. Status rechecking is distinct from granting permission.
Outcome/application/constraint framing and checking the requested application and action are recommended. App Tool Permissions determine approval prompts and session versus persistent grants.
Stop or one Escape press interrupts the current app operation; this differs from the CLI's two-Escape instruction.
Persistent application approval is shared between app and CLI on the same computer. Removing it only changes future sessions and does not revoke an existing session grant.
Stopping the current operation and ending its session are distinct: ending the session revokes access granted to that session, according to the source.
Settings and the session command provide feature-disablement entry points; no settings or permissions were changed during review.
Account/platform availability and two separately granted macOS prerequisites require confirmation; absent controls cannot be represented as successful enablement.
